claims.text: Engineering the precursors to have similar decomposition activation energies will cause nearly simultaneous release of the constituent metal atoms during nucleation.
Nearly simultaneous metal-atom release will promote homogeneous formation of a single-phase solid solution.
Asynchronous precursor decomposition will cause phase separation or elemental segregation.
The proposed nanoparticle system contains Au, Pt, Pd, Rh, and Ir precursors.
Ligand selection can tune all precursor decomposition events into a 20–30 °C temperature window.
Narrowly distributed precursor decomposition profiles produce a uniform nucleation event.
Uniform nucleation minimizes local compositional fluctuations.
Reduced local compositional fluctuations favor a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
Early nucleation of one metal relative to the others promotes phase separation or elemental segregation.
Synchronized precursors will produce nanoparticles with more uniform elemental distributions than conventional unsynchronized precursors.
Synchronized precursors will produce the targeted single-phase crystal structure, whereas unsynchronized precursors will produce multiphase microstructures.
Conventional precursor sets with widely separated decomposition temperatures generally yield multiphase products and elemental segregation under rapid heating and cooling.
The proposed mechanism applies under rapid heating–cooling regimes when precursor decomposition occurs within a narrow temperature window.
Uniform heating and reliable tuning of ligand-dependent decomposition kinetics are necessary boundaries for the hypothesis.
